subject: Mutual Action Plan: Brightline evaluation & owners (MAP v1)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hammond <claire@brightline.ai>, Ken Lopez <klopez@brightline.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: Brightline evaluation & owners (MAP v1)

Hi Claire / Ken —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday and for outlining the three evaluation goals: latency under 200ms p50, top-5 intent accuracy >= 92% on your benchmark prompts, and a 35% token-cost reduction vs your current hosted endpoint. To keep momentum and hit a target procurement + pilot signature by July 21, I sketched a short MAP and assigned owners for the evaluation workstreams.

High-level timeline (proposed)
- Week 1 (Jul 1–7): MAP alignment, prompt set finalization, infra access + test credentials
- Week 2 (Jul 8–14): Run benchmark suite across 3 model configs; collect latency/cost/eval metrics
- Week 3 (Jul 15–21): Quality review, remediation prompts, runway for procurement review and signatures

Success criteria (initial)
- Latency: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 450ms for 512-token average sequences
- Quality: top-5 intent accuracy >= 92% on seed prompt set
- Cost: <= 65% of current per-token spend on your baseline

Owners (Redwood)
- Evaluation owner / prompts & metrics: Marissa Cole (marissa@redwood.com) — will coordinate prompt sets and evaluation harness
- Engineering lead (runtime configs & access): Rafael Mendes (rafael@redwood.com) — will provision test instances and run workloads
- Commercial / contract: Sean Gallagher (sean@redwood.com) — will coordinate procurement milestones and pricing

Brightline owners — please confirm who will: (1) sign off on the prompt set & success criteria, (2) provide test credentials for the staging data, and (3) own procurement reviews.

I've attached a spreadsheet (Brightline_MAP_v1.xlsx) that breaks down week-by-week owners, acceptance gates, and the minimal deliverables for each gate. Also included is a small prompt set for initial benchmarking (benchmark_prompt_set.md).

Next steps
1) Claire / Ken: confirm owners and any edits to the success criteria by EOD Jul 3
2) Rafael: once owners are confirmed, I’ll share a short runbook and credentials template
3) Sean: I’ll flag the commercial checklist for your review (pricing band options, SLA requests)

Thanks — excited to get this in motion.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: 2026-07-02T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: Brightline evaluation & owners (MAP v1)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan and spreadsheet. Quick confirmations from our side:
1) Owners at Brightline
   - Evaluation / success criteria sign-off: Claire Hammond (me)
   - Technical access / staging data: Ken Lopez (klopez@brightline.ai)
   - Procurement / contracting: procurement@brightline.ai (for negotiations and PO)

2) Prompt set: we’ll add ~30 additional customer-style prompts to your benchmark_prompt_set.md by Jul 4. Expect a short CSV today with the first 10 sample prompts.

3) Timing: Jul 21 target looks good, but if initial runs indicate significant quality drift we’ll need an additional week; please call this out in the acceptance gates.

Question for Rafael: for the latency runs, do you need any synthetic load generator or will you instrument against our staging traffic? We prefer to validate against anonymized staging traces if that’s possible — we can provide temporary read-only keys.

Thanks — I’ll confirm when we push the CSV.

— Claire
Claire Hammond
Head of Product | Brightline AI
claire@brightline.ai
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hammond <claire@brightline.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ken Lopez <klopez@brightline.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-03T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: Brightline evaluation & owners (MAP v1)

Thanks Claire — read-only staging keys for anonymized traces are ideal. That lets us run the same request distribution and preserves fidelity for latency/cost comparisons. We’ll do both: a synthetic generator to stress test tail latency and the staging traces for realistic P50/P95 numbers.

Quick notes on instrumentation and outputs we’ll deliver:
- We'll produce a single CSV per run: prompt_id, model_variant, p50_ms, p95_ms, avg_tokens, token_cost_usd, deterministic_score, top5_intent_flag
- We’ll publish the CSVs to the shared Drive folder and add a short README describing measurement methodology
- If we hit >5% quality regression vs your seed set we’ll open a remediation item and log it in the MAP spreadsheet

Marissa — I’ll provision the test model configs (3 variants) today and send SSH/API keys to Ken by EOD Jul 3.

Rafael Mendes
Principal Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com

Claire / procurement team —

Looping in procurement as requested. A couple of commercial items to note as we move toward the Jul 21 target:
- Pilot pricing: we can offer a capped pilot spend of $8,000 for 3 weeks with usage reporting. If you exceed, we notify and pause until approvals are in place.
- SLA / data handling: we will include a temporary pilot addendum that narrows retention to 7 days and restricts logs to the trial workspace. We can provide SOC2 evidence on request.
- DocuSign: I’ll drop a pilot addendum link into the Drive folder once you confirm the PO owner.

Claire — once you confirm procurement contact and the PO cadence, I’ll prepare the DocuSign and get finance prepped.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth MAP run and a clear go/no-go by Jul 21.
